Behind the motion.

A mechanical sculpture inspired by watch movements and robotics, with scenes that connect to my projects. The models and choreography were built for this site.

References

  • Lusion — the visual reference for a generous editorial layout, glossy sculptural objects, and motion that drives the page.
  • Lusion’s WebGL Scroll Sync — its MIT-licensed example informed the single-canvas approach: measure DOM frames, map the camera to each frame, and clip the scene to its visible area.
  • Three.js physical materials and clearcoat example — reflective cobalt, brushed metal, and enamel materials.
  • Codrops: glass and plastic in Three.js — material and lighting research for the scene.

Libraries

Three.js, including its MIT-licensed RoomEnvironment and RoundedBoxGeometry, provides the renderer, lighting environment, and geometry. GSAP, ScrollTrigger, and SplitText handle entrances, heading reveals, and the project sequence.

No Lusion images, models, or site assets are reused. Motion can be paused, and small screens use a natural vertical layout.
